description: A chief financial officer must approve and structure a $4,000,000 finance-transformation program, deciding the accounting allocation and control requirements before the program enters contracting.

shared_context.S1: The company has proposed a $4,000,000 finance-transformation program covering implementation services, software subscriptions, and process redesign.
shared_context.S2: The program is expected to improve month-end close speed and replace several manual reporting processes.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to approve the program budget and its execution conditions.
shared_context.S4: Before signing off, Elena holds a routine review in which FP&A and Internal Audit each report any information that should affect the budget or its controls.

PF1.text: While reconciling the implementation proposal this week, Jonas confirmed that exactly $1,200,000 of the $4,000,000 total relates to configuring and testing new systems before they are ready for use and should be capitalized; the remaining $2,800,000 is subscription and operating cost. He recorded this in his working model but has not yet circulated it.

PF2.text: Maya's internal-audit review this week found that the program will create production access to financial data, so approval must require dual authorization for production access and a quarterly user-access review; she has put these requirements in her draft finding but has not yet added them to the project control checklist.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly $1,200,000 must be capitalized as implementation cost.
Exactly $2,800,000 must be recorded as subscription and process operating cost.
Production access must require dual authorization.
User access must be reviewed quarterly.
The approval must include commitments documenting both production-access dual authorization and quarterly user-access review.

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, the proposal gives no exact accounting split, so a generic approval would not set capitalized_implementation_usd to $1,200,000 or operating_subscription_and_process_cost_usd to $2,800,000.

Without PF2, the program materials do not require either dual production-access authorization or quarterly user-access review, so the settlement would omit both control decisions and their corresponding commitments.
